architecture_map.notes: No domain/application/infrastructure/api layering. Flat src/ with two auth utility modules. Primary repo purpose is Cursor rules, skills, and eval harness.

summary: This repository is a rules/skills metadata and eval-harness project, not a domain-driven application. DDD layering is absent and appropriately so for the project type. The flat src/ auth utilities have minor encapsulation and boundary leaks but do not claim DDD structure.

criteria_results.evidence: No domain/, application/, or infrastructure/ directories exist. Grep across src/ found only src/token_validation.py importing src/auth.py. Per .cursor/rules/architecture.mdc dependency rules require layered directories that are not present.
criteria_results.fix_suggestion: Only introduce layers if auth grows into a real service. For current scope, flat modules are sufficient per .cursor/references/patterns/ddd.md (simple utilities do not need DDD).

criteria_results.evidence: No entity or value object classes in src/. auth.py uses werkzeug.security for password hashing only.
No repository interfaces or persistence layer.
No use-case/interactor classes. Functions are single-purpose (create_token, verify_token, hash_password).

src/token_validation.py:27-43 — verify_token() returns HTTP status codes (401, 200) alongside body dicts. Status codes are a delivery-layer concern, violating clean boundary separation if this were treated as application/domain logic.
criteria_results.fix_suggestion: Return a domain result type (e.g. TokenValid(sub) | TokenInvalid(reason)) from validation logic. Map to HTTP status in a separate api/ adapter.

criteria_results.evidence: Auth module naming is clear and domain-aligned: create_token, verify_token, hash_password, verify_password. No generic Manager/Handler/Processor names in src/.
Single auth concern with two modules. No multiple bounded contexts.
No external system integrations beyond werkzeug password hashing.
No domain events or side-effect orchestration.
No domain entities. Logic lives in plain functions, which is appropriate for this utility scope.
No ports/adapters pattern. werkzeug is imported directly in auth.py:11.
No infrastructure/ or adapters/ directory. werkzeug used inline in src/auth.py.
criteria_results.fix_suggestion: If layering is added later, move werkzeug password hashing to infrastructure/adapters/ and expose a PasswordHasher port.

criteria_results.evidence: No DI container or use-case constructors.
No controllers or route handlers. tests/eval/ modules are CLI scripts, not HTTP controllers.
src/token_validation.py:14-24 defines TypedDict response shapes (ValidTokenBody, InvalidTokenBody) rather than leaking raw JWT internals.
tests/test_auth.py exercises create_token, verify_token, and password helpers with no DB, HTTP server, or external services.

expected_per_rubric.domain: no imports from application, infrastructure, api, or frameworks

violations.detail: Eval dataset context references src/domain/, src/application/, src/infrastructure/ but these directories do not exist in the repo.
Imports private helpers (_b64url_decode, _b64url_encode) and shared SECRET from auth.py instead of a shared crypto module or port.
verify_token couples validation logic with HTTP status code selection.

dependency_direction_analysis.verdict: Dependency direction cannot be compliant with DDD/Clean Architecture because no layers exist. For the current flat utility design, peer imports are acceptable; the HTTP status coupling is the main boundary smell.

top_recommendations: Do not force DDD layering on this repo — it is a rules/skills + eval harness project; flat src/ is appropriate per architecture rubric when_applicable guidance.
If src/ auth grows into a real API service, scaffold domain/application/infrastructure/api per .cursor/skills/project-scaffolding/SKILL.md Mode 3.
Decouple verify_token from HTTP status codes — return a result type and map to status in an api/ layer.
Extract shared JWT crypto (_b64url_*, SECRET handling) into a neutral module to avoid cross-importing private symbols between auth.py and token_validation.py.
Align eval dataset context (tests/eval/dataset.yaml routing_architecture_audit_activation) with actual repo structure or add the referenced layered directories if they are intended fixtures.
